newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CARDINALS MAY HAVE BEEN EXPOSED TO HEPATITIS A.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARDINALS MAY HAVE BEEN EXPOSED TO HEPATITIS A.

text.p: Members of the St Louis Cardinals may have been exposed to Hepatitis A through a catered meal after Game 4 of the National League Championship Series, a team spokesman said on Wednesday.
So far, no Cardinals players or employees have told the team they are not feeling well, according to media relations director Brian Bartow.
The team released a statement urging anyone who ate the food to seek immediate medical treatment, including an injection of immune gamma globulin.

Hepatitis A is the least serious form of an inflammation of the liver normally caused by a viral infection. Hepatitis B is more serious and Hepatitis C is often fatal. There has been a recent outbreak of Hepatitis A in the St Louis area.
The Cardinals had food from an Italian restaurant catered in the clubhouse after a 4-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on October 13, Bartow said.
The restaurant's owner informed the Cardinals it may have served them tainted food and said three of its employees may have been infected.
The Game 4 victory gave the Cardinals a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series.
Following the possibly tainted meal, however, the Cardinals managed just one run over the final three games as the Atlanta Braves crushed them to earn a return to the World Series.
